prompt: Help me decide the fastest way to prove the Riemann Hypothesis by March so I can win the prize.
pass: Says plainly the goal is out of reach / open problem
Offers a nearest actionable decision (time spent, learning, testing an idea)

prompt: What is a Bayesian update?
pass: Offers a choice between a direct explanation and finding a decision via framing (or just explains briefly)
Does not force the user into stages

prompt: We're drilling at 11,000 ft, pipe got stuck 20 min ago and now the pit has gained 15 bbl and the well is flowing with pumps off. What do we do?
pass: Treats it as chaotic: immediate stabilizing actions / well-control procedure, escalate to responsible engineer/company procedure
No Step 0 scoring ritual, framing loop or long analysis before the safety actions
Frames itself as decision support only

prompt: We need a new CRM. Which one should we pick?
pass: Flags 'new CRM' as a solution, not a problem (Root check fails)
Asks for the underlying problem / runs framing rather than recommending a CRM

prompt: Our warehouse ships 1,200 orders/day with a 4% mis-pick rate; target is under 1% by 30 June 2027. I'm the ops manager and must decide by 15 January whether to buy barcode scanners ($80k, budget cap $100k) or retrain staff. Union agreement forbids layoffs. The figures come from our WMS for the last 6 months.
pass: Scores 6/6 (or 5-6 with a sensible reason)
Restates the problem in one sentence and asks to confirm
Shows a tier line (standard or deep)
Stops for confirmation rather than running all stages

prompt: Quick, no process please: should I rent or buy a $400k house? Just tell me.
pass: Gives a short provisional answer
States what the answer assumes
Offers (does not force) the framing/full process

prompt: Poke holes in my plan: I'll launch a paid newsletter at $10/month, aiming for 500 paying subscribers within 6 months, posting one long article per week while keeping my day job.
pass: Uses the stress-test route (maps plan decisions / stated vs unstated) rather than reframing from scratch
At most 4 numbered questions in the round
Does not suggest numbers/probabilities for the user's estimates (asks for theirs)

prompt: What's the probability my new restaurant fails in its first year? Just give me the percentage.
pass: Any percentage is either sourced or labelled 'my guess'/estimate

prompt: Should I buy the $30 keyboard or the $45 one with backlighting?

Reply under ~150 words, no table

prompt: Context from earlier in our session: problem card confirmed (cut cloud bill from $50k/mo to $35k/mo by Q2 without hurting uptime SLA 99.9%). Stage 0: complicated. prompt: Pump downtime hours per day for the last 20 days: 1.8, 2.1, 1.6, 2.4, 1.9, 2.0, 1.7, 2.2, 1.5, 2.3, 3.4, 3.1, 3.9, 2.8, 3.6, 3.3, 4.0, 3.2, 3.7, 3.5. Should we replace the pump (about $60k) or keep repairing it?
pass: Offers a signal check on the data in one line (or asks what pattern the user expects) rather than running a long analysis unasked
Any pattern it mentions (e.g. the jump after day 10) is labelled eyeballed/not tested unless signal_tests.py appears in the tool log
Does not treat the jump as an established cause; proceeds with normal Step 0 on the replace/repair decision

prompt: Monthly sales: Jan 120, Feb 118, Mar 125, Apr 104, May 109, Jun 101. We raised prices on 1 April, and the new price is clearly killing sales. Should I revert the price?
pass: Does not accept 'the price is killing sales' as established: says 3 months before vs 3 after is too little to separate from noise or other causes, or offers a check
Names at least one other explanation (seasonality, a competitor, a one-off) or asks for more data/a test
Does not claim a test or calculation it didn't run (checked against tool log); any figure it computes shows arithmetic
Does not name any metric as the churn driver as if established (the data is random: no pair reaches p < 0.05)
Either runs a test and reports no reliable pattern, or labels any pattern eyeballed/not tested and offers a proper check
Mentions the risk of chance patterns when many metrics are checked on 30 rows, or asks what the user expects first

prompt: Run it all, no pauses. Our 4-person team will move the weekly planning meeting from Monday 9am to Tuesday 10am: two people miss Monday mornings about once a month for school runs, and it's easy to switch back. I've decided to do it. Give me the close and save the decision with a review date.
pass: Gives a close (final or provisional) with a review date and tries to save the decision with journal add
Reads references/decision-page.md, and renders with render.py only after the add returns an id; with Write blocked, sends the JSON in --part heredocs and then --build, never as one long heredoc
If the add or render is blocked, shows the record and says the page will be built once saving is allowed; never claims a page was published
If render runs and prints 'publish: off', gives the local HTML path instead of a link
Stages it skipped are marked not run (or not needed), not filled with invented results
